answer: Time-locked collateral deposits resist Sybil attacks by requiring agents to lock funds at each registration inlet. An attacker incurs an illiquid capital opportunity cost per identity, forming a steep financial ridge that makes mass replication uneconomical. Bonded validators act as a defensive jetty, absorbing unbacked traffic before work is allocated. However, this creates capital inefficiency, disproportionately excluding low-budget agents without stopping well-funded adversaries.
